article.story: OXFORD, Miss. -- — Blake Purchase’s interception return to the 1 set up a short touchdown run by quarterback Trinidad Chambliss, and No. 23 Mississippi rallied past Mississippi State 41-17 Friday. Chambliss ran around left end for a 27-17 lead with 10:30 left in the game as true separation began. He also threw two touchdown passes, and running back Joshua Dye ran for two touchdowns, all after halftime as the Rebels turned back an upset bid from their beleaguered rival. The Bulldogs have not won a game against an FBS team since an injury to star quarterback Kamario Taylor against Alabama in Week 5. Ole Miss (8-4, 5-4 SEC) began the day as a 17.5-point favorite. “I really challenged them at halftime, and to go 35-7 in the second half in that rivalry ...," Ole Miss coach Pete Golding said. "It’s always great to win regardless, always good to beat your rival in the last regular-season game and give us a little bit momentum going into bowl game.” The Bulldogs were only three points back and driving when Purchase got the pick. “That was the difference in the game," Mississippi State coach Jeff Lebby said. "We got back in it, were on the plus-41, and the kid makes an incredible play. It was frustrating.” Golding agreed. “You felt that momentum starting to slide, then to come back and change the game … that was the dagger,” he said. After Dye’s 4-yard run gave Ole Miss a 20-10 lead with 4:45 left in the third, the Bulldogs (5-7, 2-7 SEC) answered on Billy Puckett’s 12-yard pass to running back Fluff Bothwell. Bothwell earlier scored on a 16-yard run in the first quarter, and State led 10-6 at halftime. Chambliss passed 6 yards to Horatio Fields to give the Rebels their first lead, 13-10, with 9:53 left in the third. A personal foul and defensive holding calls helped boost State to a 40-yard field goal and a 10-6 lead with 1:48 left in the first half. A scattering of Ole Miss fans booed as the Bulldogs forced Chambliss to take check-down routes and burn time on a 2-minute drill that ended when kicker Lucas Carneiro missed from 62 yards. Mississippi State defensive coordinator Zach Arnett showed Chambliss a variety of looks in the first half. Chambliss said he wasn’t rattled. “We were shooting ourselves in the foot. The plays were there," he said. "It was only a matter of time, and the plays were going to go our way.” Run game revival The Rebels have struggled to run consistently after an early-season injury to starting running back Kewan Lacy, who the school in August promoted for the Heisman along with Chambliss. It took the Rebels into the second half to spark the run game, but Dye, once the fourth running back on the depth chart, finished with 96 yards on 20 carries. Ole Miss had 118 rushing yards, with only Chambliss and wide receiver Deuce Alexander as the other rushers. The Takeaway Mississippi State: Because of four wins earned with Taylor at quarterback, the Bulldogs, who defeated FCS Tennessee Tech last week, would have been bowl-eligible had they sprung a historic upset. Mississippi: Ole Miss has won four straight and six of the last seven in the series known as the Egg Bowl. Poll Implications Ole Miss expects to remain ranked for a 64th-straight week, it’s longest run since 73 weeks from 1957-64. Up next Mississippi State: Season over. Ole Miss: Bowl game TBD. ------ Sign up for Top 25 poll alerts here, visit the Top 25 here and see AP’s full college football coverage here
